fstestrun.desc: The test package's runner: check, copy, flash, boot, wait, verdict, clean up
fstestrun.body:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Kotl FireSim test: boot Linux on the FPGA and power it off. Needs nothing but this folder:
# no Chipyard, no FireSim install, no conda. Run it through Kotl, from any folder you can write to:
#
#   kotl run --eta 15m -- /path/to/kotl-firesim-test/run.sh
#
# What it does, as you, with only your job's key (KOTL_PC, set by Kotl inside the job):
#   1. checks the board's PC: Xilinx card, XDMA loaded with poll_mode=1, xvsec, xvsecctl, sudo
#   2. copies payload/ to the PC (~/kotl-firesim-test-JOB)
#   3. flashes the FPGA with the bitstream (sudo xvsecctl), the way FireSim's infrasetup does
#   4. runs the FireSim driver in screen session fsim0 (kotl attach shows the console),
#      the way FireSim's runworkload does, using the PC's own glibc
#   5. waits for the simulated Linux to power off (or the time limit), copies the uartlog back
#   6. removes its folder on the PC, and prints KOTL RESULT: PASS only on "reboot: Power down"
#
# It prints 'KOTL FACT: key=value' lines (from MANIFEST: what the package was built from), so its
# line in the lab notes (kotl notes firesim) says which bitstream and driver ran.
# Results: ./firesim-test-results/JOB/ (uartlog, and the driver's other logs).
# Settings (environment): KOTL_TEST_TIMEOUT (seconds, default 900), KOTL_TEST_KEEP=1 keeps the
# folder on the PC, KOTL_TEST_OUT (results folder).
set -uo pipefail
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
JOB=${KOTL_JOB:-manual-$$}
OUT=${KOTL_TEST_OUT:-$PWD/firesim-test-results/$JOB}
TIMEOUT=${KOTL_TEST_TIMEOUT:-900}
DIR="kotl-firesim-test-$JOB"             # on the PC, in the board account's home
step() { echo; echo "== $(date +%H:%M:%S) $*"; }
fail() { echo "KOTL RESULT: FAIL ($*)"; exit 1; }
pc() { ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=15 "$KOTL_PC" "$@"; }
who_connected() {   # workstation accounts with an SSH connection to the PC now (the kernel's table)
  local ip=${KOTL_PC#*@} hex
  hex=$(echo "$ip" | awk -F. 'NF == 4 { printf "%02X%02X%02X%02X:0016", $4, $3, $2, $1 }')
  [ -n "$hex" ] || return 0
  awk -v h="$hex" 'NR > 1 && $3 == h && $4 == "01" { print $8 }' /proc/net/tcp 2>/dev/null | sort | uniq -c |
    while read -r n uid; do u=$(getent passwd "$uid" | cut -d: -f1); [ "$u" = kotl ] || printf '%s%s ' "${u:-uid $uid}" "$([ "$n" -gt 1 ] && echo " ($n)")"; done
}

[ -n "${KOTL_PC:-}" ] || fail "run me inside a Kotl job: kotl run --eta 15m -- $0"
[ -d "$HERE/payload/sim" ] && [ -f "$HERE/payload/bitstream/firesim.bit" ] || fail "payload/ is incomplete; rebuild the package"
mkdir -p "$OUT" || fail "can't write results to $OUT (run from a folder you can write to, or set KOTL_TEST_OUT)"
. "$HERE/payload/sim/args.sh"            # SIM_ARGS: the driver's arguments (from the FireSim run it came from)

# what this package is, for the lab notes (kotl notes firesim: runs.md)
facts() {
  local m="$HERE/MANIFEST"
  echo "KOTL FACT: tool=firesim"
  echo "KOTL FACT: package=$HERE"
  [ -f "$m" ] || return 0
  sed -n '1s/.*built \([0-9-]*\).*/KOTL FACT: package_built=\1/p' "$m"
  sed -n 's#^chipyard: *\([^ ]*\)$#KOTL FACT: chipyard=\1#p; s#^firesim: *\([^ ]*\)$#KOTL FACT: firesim=\1#p' "$m"
  sed -n 's#^bitstream: .*/\([^/]*\)/[^/]*$#KOTL FACT: bitstream=\1#p' "$m"
  sed -n 's#^driver: .*/\([^/]*\)/[^/]*$#KOTL FACT: driver=\1#p' "$m"
  sed -n 's#^workload: *[^ ]*/\([^/ ]*\) .*#KOTL FACT: workload=\1#p' "$m"
  awk '$2 == "payload/bitstream/firesim.bit" { print "KOTL FACT: bit_sha256=" substr($1, 1, 12) }' "$m"
}
facts

step "1/6 checking the board's PC ($KOTL_PC)"
PC_CHECK=$(cat <<'EOF'
set -e
card=$(lspci -nd 10ee: | head -n 1)
[ -n "$card" ] || { echo "no Xilinx card on PCI"; exit 1; }
echo "card: $card"
if screen -ls 2>/dev/null | grep -q '\.fsim0'; then
  echo "OUTSIDE KOTL: FireSim is already running on the PC, and it isn't a Kotl job:"
  screen -ls 2>/dev/null | grep '\.fsim' | awk '{print "  screen " $1}'
  ps -eo user,etime,comm 2>/dev/null | awk '$3 ~ /^FireSim-/ { print "  driver running for " $2 " (as " $1 ")" }'
  echo "BUSY-OUTSIDE"
  exit 1
fi
lsmod | grep -q '^xdma ' || { echo "the XDMA driver isn't loaded (Kotl's health check reloads it on an idle board)"; exit 1; }
pm=$(cat /sys/module/xdma/parameters/poll_mode 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
[ "$pm" = 1 ] || { echo "XDMA is loaded with poll_mode=$pm; FireSim needs 1 (admin: sudo /usr/local/bin/kotl-xdma-reload on an idle board)"; exit 1; }
lsmod | grep -q '^xvsec ' || { echo "the xvsec driver isn't loaded (needed to flash the FPGA)"; exit 1; }
command -v xvsecctl >/dev/null || { echo "xvsecctl isn't installed on the PC"; exit 1; }
sudo -n true 2>/dev/null || { echo "the board account can't use sudo without a password (FireSim needs it)"; exit 1; }
echo "ok: XDMA poll_mode=1, xvsec, xvsecctl, sudo"
EOF
)
check=$(pc bash -s <<<"$PC_CHECK" 2>&1); ok=$?
echo "$check" | grep -v '^BUSY-OUTSIDE$'
if [ $ok -ne 0 ]; then
  if echo "$check" | grep -q '^BUSY-OUTSIDE$'; then
    who=$(who_connected)
    echo "  connected to the PC from the workstation now: ${who:-nobody (a leftover, or started and left running)}"
    echo "  Kotl leaves it running. Ask them to use kotl run / kotl lease, then run this test again."
    fail "FireSim is running on the board outside Kotl"
  fi
  fail "the board's PC isn't ready (see above)"
fi

step "2/6 copying the package to the PC (~/$DIR)"
tar -C "$HERE/payload" -cf - . | pc "rm -rf '$DIR' && mkdir -p '$DIR' && tar -C '$DIR' -xf -" || fail "copying to the PC"

cleanup() {
  [ "${KOTL_TEST_KEEP:-0}" = 1 ] && { echo "keeping ~/$DIR on the PC (KOTL_TEST_KEEP=1)"; return; }
  pc "rm -rf '$DIR'" && echo "removed ~/$DIR on the PC"
}

step "3/6 flashing the FPGA"
pc "cd '$DIR' && set -- \$(lspci -nd 10ee: | head -n 1) && bdf=\$1 && bus=\${bdf%%:*} && dev=\${bdf#*:} && dev=\${dev%%.*} &&
    sudo xvsecctl -b 0x\$bus -F 0x\$dev -c 0x1 -p bitstream/firesim.bit" || { cleanup; fail "flashing the FPGA"; }

step "4/6 starting the simulation (screen fsim0; watch it with: kotl attach)"
pc "cd '$DIR/sim' && set -- \$(lspci -nd 10ee: | head -n 1) && bdf=\$1 && id=\$3 && bus=\${bdf%%:*} && rest=\${bdf#*:} && dev=\${rest%%.*} && fn=\${bdf##*.} &&
    screen -S fsim0 -d -m bash -c \"script -f -c 'stty intr ^] && sudo ./FireSim-xilinx_vcu118 $SIM_ARGS +domain=0x0000 +bus=0x\$bus +device=0x\$dev +function=0x\$fn +bar=0x0 +pci-vendor=0x10ee +pci-device=0x\${id#*:} +permissive-off +prog0=poweroffnode-br-base-bin && stty intr ^c' uartlog\" && sleep 2 &&
    screen -ls | grep -q '\.fsim0'" || { cleanup; fail "starting the FireSim driver"; }

step "5/6 waiting for Linux to boot and power off (up to $((TIMEOUT / 60)) min)"
start=$(date +%s); last=""
while pc "screen -ls 2>/dev/null | grep -q '\.fsim0'"; do
  now=$(date +%s)
  line=$(pc "tail -n 1 '$DIR/sim/uartlog' 2>/dev/null" | tr -d '\r' | cut -c1-120)
  [ -n "$line" ] && [ "$line" != "$last" ] && { echo "  [$((now - start))s] $line"; last=$line; }
  if [ $((now - start)) -ge "$TIMEOUT" ]; then
    echo "  time limit reached: stopping the simulation"
    pc "screen -S fsim0 -X quit; sudo pkill -f 'FireSim-xilinx' || true"
    break
  fi
  sleep 10
done
pc "cat '$DIR/sim/uartlog'" > "$OUT/uartlog" 2>/dev/null
for f in blkdev-log0 niclog0; do pc "cat '$DIR/sim/$f' 2>/dev/null" > "$OUT/$f" || rm -f "$OUT/$f"; done
cleanup

step "6/6 result"
echo "--- uartlog (last lines): $OUT/uartlog"
tail -n 8 "$OUT/uartlog" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r'
if grep -aqs "reboot: Power down" "$OUT/uartlog"; then
  echo "KOTL RESULT: PASS"
else
  fail "the simulated Linux did not power off; see $OUT/uartlog"
fi

fstestmake.name: make-test-package.sh
fstestmake.desc: Builds the test package from a Chipyard, reading it only
fstestmake.body:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the Kotl FireSim test package: one self-contained folder that boots Linux on a VCU118
# through Kotl, for users with no Chipyard. Reads a Chipyard (never changes it), writes OUT.
#
#   make-test-package.sh --chipyard ~/chipyard --out /shared/kotl-firesim-test
#
# Defaults are the combination that booted Linux on vcu118-pc1 (Kotl job 49): the
# xilinx_vcu118_firesim_rocket_singlecore_4GB_no_nic bitstream, its FireSimRocket32KBL1NoL2Config
# driver, and the linux-poweroff workload. Override with --bitstream-tar, --driver-dir,
# --workload-dir, --sim-run (a sim-run.sh FireSim generated, for the driver's arguments).
#
# The folder: run.sh, README.md, MANIFEST (sources and sha256), payload/{bitstream,sim}.
# The driver bundle ships WITHOUT the workstation's glibc, so the PC's own glibc is used.
set -euo pipefail
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
CY="" OUT=""
BIT="" DRV="" WL="" SIMRUN="" IMG=""
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --chipyard) CY=$2; shift ;;
    --out) OUT=$2; shift ;;
    --bitstream-tar) BIT=$2; shift ;;
    --driver-dir) DRV=$2; shift ;;
    --workload-dir) WL=$2; shift ;;
    --sim-run) SIMRUN=$2; shift ;;
    -h|--help) sed -n '2,14p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "unknown option $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
  shift
done
[ -n "$CY" ] && [ -n "$OUT" ] || { echo "usage: $0 --chipyard PATH --out DIR" >&2; exit 2; }
FS="$CY/sims/firesim"
BIT=${BIT:-$FS/deploy/results-build/ref-2026-06-03-xilinx_vcu118_firesim_rocket_singlecore_4GB_no_nic/firesim.tar.gz}
DRV=${DRV:-$FS/sim/output/xilinx_vcu118/xilinx_vcu118-firesim-FireSim-FireSimRocket32KBL1NoL2Config-BaseXilinxVCU118Config}
WL=${WL:-$FS/deploy/workloads/linux-poweroff}
IMG="$FS/sw/firesim-software/images/firechip/br-base"
SIMRUN=${SIMRUN:-$(ls -t "$FS"/deploy/results-workload/*linux-poweroff/poweroffnode/sim-run.sh 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)}
for f in "$BIT" "$DRV/driver-bundle.tar.gz" "$WL/poweroffnode.ext2" "$WL/br-base-bin" "$IMG/br-base-bin-dwarf" "$SIMRUN"; do
  [ -e "$f" ] || { echo "missing: $f" >&2; exit 1; }
done
case "$(cd "$(dirname "$OUT")" && pwd)/$(basename "$OUT")/" in "$(cd "$CY" && pwd)/"*) echo "--out must be outside the Chipyard" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac

tmp="$OUT.partial"
rm -rf "$tmp"
mkdir -p "$tmp/payload/bitstream" "$tmp/payload/sim"
echo "bitstream: $BIT"
tar -xzf "$BIT" -C "$tmp/payload/bitstream" --strip-components=1 xilinx_vcu118/firesim.bit xilinx_vcu118/metadata
echo "driver:    $DRV/driver-bundle.tar.gz (without the workstation's glibc)"
tar -xzf "$DRV/driver-bundle.tar.gz" -C "$tmp/payload/sim" --exclude=libc.so.6 --exclude=libm.so.6 \
  --exclude=libpthread.so.0 --exclude=libdl.so.2 --exclude=librt.so.1
echo "workload:  $WL (linux-poweroff)"
cp -L "$WL/poweroffnode.ext2" "$tmp/payload/sim/poweroffnode-poweroffnode.ext2"
cp -L "$WL/br-base-bin" "$tmp/payload/sim/poweroffnode-br-base-bin"
cp -L "$IMG/br-base-bin-dwarf" "$tmp/payload/sim/poweroffnode-br-base-bin-dwarf"
# the driver's own arguments, as FireSim generated them; the PCI address is found on the PC
args=$(grep -o "sudo ./FireSim-xilinx_vcu118 [^&']*" "$SIMRUN" | sed 's#^sudo ./FireSim-xilinx_vcu118 ##; s# +domain=.*##; s#  *# #g; s# *$##')
[ -n "$args" ] || { echo "no driver arguments found in $SIMRUN" >&2; exit 1; }
printf '# the FireSim driver arguments (from %s)\nSIM_ARGS="%s"\n' "$SIMRUN" "$args" >"$tmp/payload/sim/args.sh"
cp "$HERE/test-package/run.sh" "$tmp/run.sh"
abs_out="$(cd "$(dirname "$OUT")" && pwd)/$(basename "$OUT")"
sed "s#@PACKAGE@#$abs_out#g" "$HERE/test-package/README.md" >"$tmp/README.md"
chmod 755 "$tmp/run.sh" "$tmp/payload/sim/FireSim-xilinx_vcu118"
{
  echo "Kotl FireSim test package, built $(date -Is) by $(id -un) on $(hostname -s)"
  echo "bitstream: $BIT"
  echo "driver:    $DRV/driver-bundle.tar.gz"
  echo "workload:  $WL + $IMG/br-base-bin-dwarf"
  echo "args from: $SIMRUN"
  echo "chipyard:  $(git -C "$CY" rev-parse --short=10 HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo '?')"
  echo "firesim:   $(git -C "$FS" rev-parse --short=10 HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo '?')"
  echo
  (cd "$tmp" && find payload run.sh README.md -type f -print0 | sort -z | xargs -0 sha256sum)
} >"$tmp/MANIFEST"
chmod -R a+rX "$tmp"
rm -rf "$OUT"
mv "$tmp" "$OUT"
echo "built $OUT ($(du -sh "$OUT" | cut -f1)); anyone can read it. Try: kotl run --eta 15m -- $OUT/run.sh"

fsstop.name: kotl-firesim-stop
fsstop.desc: FireSim adapter: the end step's root cleanup; stops FireSim drivers (they run as root)
fsstop.body:
#!/bin/sh
# managed by kotl (deploy/adapters/firesim/pc-setup.sh). FireSim adapter. Installed on each FPGA PC
# as /usr/local/bin/kotl-firesim-stop.
#
#   kotl-firesim-stop [MAX_AGE]     (as root, through one sudoers line)
#
# Kotl's end step runs it after a job's key is removed: FireSim runs its driver through sudo, so
# the driver runs as root and the board account can't stop it. It stops FireSim drivers (matched
# by process name) that started during the job: younger than MAX_AGE seconds (the job's age, so
# the PC's own clock doesn't matter). Older drivers aren't the job's: they are left and reported.
# Without MAX_AGE it stops every FireSim driver. It changes nothing else.
set -u
case "$#:${1:-0}" in 0:*|1:[0-9]*) ;; *) echo "usage: kotl-firesim-stop [MAX_AGE_SECONDS]" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
case "${1:-0}" in *[!0-9]*) echo "usage: kotl-firesim-stop [MAX_AGE_SECONDS]" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
MAX=${1:-}
drivers() { ps -eo pid=,etimes=,comm= | awk -v max="$MAX" '$3 ~ /^FireSim-/ && (max == "" || $2 <= max) { print $1 }'; }
older() { ps -eo pid=,etimes=,comm= | awk -v max="$MAX" 'max != "" && $3 ~ /^FireSim-/ && $2 > max { print $1 "(" $2 "s)" }'; }
left=$(older | paste -sd' ' -)
pids=$(drivers | paste -sd' ' -)
[ -n "$left" ] && echo "kotl-firesim-stop: left running (older than this job, outside Kotl): $left"
if [ -z "$pids" ]; then
  echo "kotl-firesim-stop: no FireSim driver of this job running"
  exit 0
fi
echo "kotl-firesim-stop: stopping: $pids"
env kill -TERM $pids 2>/dev/null || true
for _ in 1 2 3 4 5; do
  [ -z "$(drivers)" ] && { echo "kotl-firesim-stop: stopped"; exit 0; }
  sleep 1
done
env kill -KILL $(drivers) 2>/dev/null || true
sleep 1
[ -z "$(drivers)" ] || { echo "kotl-firesim-stop: a FireSim driver is still running"; exit 1; }
echo "kotl-firesim-stop: stopped (killed)"

claudemd.desc: Kotl's rules, read by every Claude Code session on the workstation
claudemd.body:
<!-- managed by kotl (deploy/kotl/install.sh). Read by every Claude Code session on this workstation. -->
# The lab's FPGA boards are shared through Kotl

This workstation's FPGA boards (VCU118 and their PCs, e.g. `vcu118-pc1`) are shared by everyone
through Kotl, a queue. Before anything that uses a board (FireSim `infrasetup`/`runworkload`,
flashing a bitstream, a driver test, ssh to an FPGA PC), go through Kotl:

- `kotl status`: the boards, the queue and who holds each board now.
- `kotl run --eta <estimate> -- <command>`: runs the command with a board, frees it after.
- `kotl lease --eta <estimate>`, then `ssh <board>`; `kotl release` when done.
- `kotl --help`; the full guide is `/opt/kotl/plugin/skills/kotl/SKILL.md` (read it first), and
  each tool has its own: FireSim's is `/opt/kotl/plugin/skills/kotl-firesim/SKILL.md`.
  `kotl setup` adds Kotl's Claude Code plugin and VS Code extension for this person.

Before running a tool on a board, read the lab notes: what worked before on these boards, with
which versions and configs (`kotl notes`, `kotl notes firesim`; the files are in
`/srv/kotl/notes/`). Afterwards add what you learned: `kotl notes add <tool> "..."`.

Never use a board outside Kotl: it can break another person's run, and Kotl can't protect work it
doesn't know about.

If a board looks busy (a FireSim `fsim*` screen or a `FireSim-*` driver on its PC) and it isn't
your Kotl job: it is someone else's work, or work outside Kotl. Don't stop it. Tell the person who
seems to run it and for how long, and that it is outside Kotl. If the person's own run outside
Kotl stopped, check `kotl status` and `kotl history`: a Kotl job may have taken the board.

updatesh.name: update.sh
updatesh.desc: Update Kotl everywhere: the workstation, then every board's PC
updatesh.body:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# managed by kotl (deploy/kotl/update.sh)
# Update Kotl everywhere from this repo, in one go. Run as the admin (not with sudo: it asks for
# sudo itself, here and on each PC), from the repo you want to install:
#
#   bash deploy/kotl/update.sh            the workstation, then every board's PC
#   bash deploy/kotl/update.sh --no-pc    the workstation only
#   bash deploy/kotl/update.sh --pc virtex-host@192.168.1.2   only that PC (repeatable)
#
# The workstation: deploy/kotl/install.sh with no options, which rebuilds and reinstalls all of
# Kotl (code, kotl command, daemon, notifier, plugins, VS Code extension, Claude rules) and keeps
# the boards and adapters already set. Each PC: Kotl's PC helpers (pc/setup.sh --keys-helper) and
# the PC part of every enabled adapter (adapters/NAME/pc-setup.sh). The PCs come from
# /etc/ssh/ssh_config.d/kotl.conf, the account from /etc/kotl/kotl.conf (pc_account).
# Users then run `kotl setup` (and reload VS Code) for the new plugins and extension.
#
# Add --dry-run to print what it would run, changing nothing.
set -uo pipefail
DEPLOY=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
REPO=$(cd "$DEPLOY/.." && pwd)
ROOT=${KOTL_ROOT:-}
DRY=0 DO_PC=1 PCS=()
say() { printf 'kotl-update: %s\n' "$*"; }
die() { printf 'kotl-update: error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
run() { if [ "$DRY" = 1 ]; then printf 'would run: %s\n' "$*"; else "$@"; fi; }
conf() { sed -n "s/^[[:space:]]*$1[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*//p" "$ROOT/etc/kotl/kotl.conf" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1; }

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --dry-run) DRY=1 ;;
    --no-pc) DO_PC=0 ;;
    --pc) PCS+=("${2:-}"); shift ;;
    -h|--help) sed -n '3,17p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
    *) die "unknown option $1" ;;
  esac
  shift
done
[ "$(id -u)" != 0 ] || [ "$DRY" = 1 ] || die "run it as yourself, not as root: it uses sudo where it needs it"

rev=$(git -C "$REPO" rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "?")
say "installing Kotl from $REPO (commit $rev)"
if [ -n "$(git -C "$REPO" status --porcelain -- kotl deploy plugin plugin-band vscode-kotl .claude-plugin 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
  say "note: the repo has uncommitted changes; they get installed too"
fi

fails=0
say "1. the workstation"
run sudo bash "$DEPLOY/kotl/install.sh" || { say "the workstation install failed: stopping"; exit 1; }

if [ "$DO_PC" = 1 ]; then
  account=$(conf pc_account); account=${account:-virtex-host}
  if [ ${#PCS[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
    while read -r addr; do PCS+=("$account@$addr"); done < <(awk '$1 == "HostName" { print $2 }' "$ROOT/etc/ssh/ssh_config.d/kotl.conf" 2>/dev/null)
  fi
  adapters=$(conf adapters | tr ',' ' ')
  parts=(pc)
  for a in $adapters; do
    case "$a" in *[!a-z0-9]*|"") die "odd adapter name in kotl.conf: '$a'" ;; esac
    [ -f "$DEPLOY/adapters/$a/pc-setup.sh" ] && parts+=("adapters/$a")
  done
  [ ${#PCS[@]} -gt 0 ] || say "no board PCs found in /etc/ssh/ssh_config.d/kotl.conf; skipping the PCs"
  for pc in "${PCS[@]}"; do
    case "$pc" in *[!A-Za-z0-9@._-]*|"") die "--pc wants USER@ADDRESS, got '$pc'" ;; esac
    say "2. the PC $pc (helpers: ${parts[*]}); it may ask for the sudo password there"
    remote="sudo bash \$d/pc/setup.sh --account $account --keys-helper \$d/pc/kotl-keys"
    for part in "${parts[@]:1}"; do remote+=" && sudo bash \$d/$part/pc-setup.sh"; done
    if [ "$DRY" = 1 ]; then
      printf 'would run: tar -C %s -cf - %s | ssh %s (into a new temporary folder)\n' "$DEPLOY" "${parts[*]}" "$pc"
      printf 'would run: ssh -t %s "%s; rm -rf the folder"\n' "$pc" "$remote"
      continue
    fi
    d=$(tar -C "$DEPLOY" -cf - "${parts[@]}" | ssh "$pc" 'd=$(mktemp -d /tmp/kotl-update.XXXXXX) && tar -C "$d" -xf - && echo "$d"') ||
      { say "couldn't copy the helpers to $pc"; fails=$((fails + 1)); continue; }
    case "$d" in /tmp/kotl-update.*) ;; *) say "odd folder from $pc: '$d'"; fails=$((fails + 1)); continue ;; esac
    ssh -t "$pc" "d=$d; $remote; rc=\$?; rm -rf \"\$d\"; exit \$rc" ||
      { say "the update on $pc failed (see above)"; fails=$((fails + 1)); continue; }
  done
fi

echo
if [ "$fails" -gt 0 ]; then say "done, with $fails PC(s) failed"; else say "done"; fi
say "users: run 'kotl setup' and reload VS Code to get the new plugins and extension"
[ "$fails" -eq 0 ]

fsskill.name: SKILL.md (kotl-firesim)
fsskill.path: plugin/skills/kotl-firesim/ (installed with the plugin when the FireSim adapter is on)
fsskill.desc: FireSim's own skill: read the lab notes first and compare the run with what worked, run FireSim through kotl run, then the notes
fsskill.body:
---
name: kotl-firesim
description: Run FireSim on the lab's FPGA boards (VCU118) through Kotl, from a Chipyard on the workstation or on the person's own PC (a run package). Use whenever a task runs FireSim (infrasetup, runworkload, a bitstream or driver from a Chipyard/FireSim build) on a board, packs a FireSim build to run it there, checks whether a build will work on the lab's boards, or asks what FireSim setup worked before. Read the kotl skill too, for the queue itself.
---

# FireSim on the lab's boards, through Kotl

Kotl's FireSim adapter keeps the boards ready for FireSim (XDMA loaded, glibc checked), stops a
run's FireSim when its job ends, and writes every FireSim run into the lab notes. The queue
itself (`kotl run`, `kotl lease`, ETAs, results) is in the **kotl** skill.

## 1. Read the lab notes first

```sh
kotl notes firesim            # setup.md, compatible.md, the latest runs, notes.md
```

Before any run, compare what the person is about to run with the notes:

- their FireSim and Chipyard commits (`git -C <chipyard> rev-parse --short=10 HEAD`, and in
  `sims/firesim`), the hardware config (`default_hw_config` in their `config_runtime.yaml`), its
  bitstream (`bitstream_tar` in `config_hwdb.yaml`), and the workload;
- against the `ok` lines in `runs.md` and the combinations in `compatible.md`.

If nothing like it has worked on these boards (another FireSim version, another shell or board
config, a bitstream built for something else), say so and what last worked, before using the
queue. If `setup.md` lists something the PC needs and the person's build expects something else
(e.g. another XDMA or Vivado version), stop and ask.

## 2. Run it

Two ways. Which one depends on where the person's Chipyard is:

| Their Chipyard is | Use |
| --- | --- |
| on their own PC (Kotl's client bundle, `KOTL_SSH` set) | **a run package** (2a): build there, pack, copy, run |
| on the workstation | **FireSim itself** (2b), or a run package too |

### 2a. A run package: build anywhere, run through Kotl (no FireSim on the workstation)

The FPGA PCs are reachable only from the workstation, so FireSim's manager can't drive a board
from the person's own PC. Instead, pack what FireSim would copy to the board's PC and let Kotl's
runner do the rest. Requirements: one simulation, no network (`topology: no_net_config`,
`no_net_num_nodes: 1`), a `xilinx_vcu118` bitstream, a workload that ends by itself.

1. Build on their PC, in their FireSim environment: the bitstream (or one they already have, in
   `config_hwdb.yaml` as a local `bitstream_tar`), `firesim builddriver -c CFG`, and the
   FireMarshal workload (`marshal build` + `marshal install`).
2. Pack it, in `sims/firesim/deploy` (on their own PC the tool is
   `~/.kotl-client/adapters/firesim/kotl-firesim-pack`; on the workstation
   `/opt/kotl/adapters/firesim/kotl-firesim-pack`):

   ```sh
   kotl-firesim-pack -c CFG --out ~/kotl-runs/NAME [--timeout 30m] [--pass REGEX]
   ```

   It reads, never changes, their FireSim. It tells you what it packed (hardware config,
   workload, driver, the glibc the driver needs) and the next two commands. If it refuses, it
   says why (no driver built, a network topology, a bitstream that isn't local, ...): fix that,
   don't work around it.
3. Copy it and run it (the eta covers copy-to-PC, flash and the simulation):

   ```sh
   rsync -a --partial ~/kotl-runs/NAME/ "$KOTL_SSH":kotl-runs/NAME/
   ssh "$KOTL_SSH" kotl run --eta 20m -- /opt/kotl/adapters/firesim/run-package.sh kotl-runs/NAME
   ```

   The runner checks the PC (and that the PC's glibc is new enough for the driver), flashes the
   bitstream, runs the driver in screen `fsim0` (`kotl attach` shows it), copies back the
   uartlog and what the run wrote, and prints `KOTL RESULT: PASS` only on a pass line
   (`*** PASSED ***` or `reboot: Power down`, or `--pass REGEX` from the pack). It prints the
   package's `KOTL FACT` lines, so the run's line in the notes says what it used.
4. Results: `ssh "$KOTL_SSH" kotl fetch JOB` (into `kotl-results/JOB/` in their workstation
   home; the uartlog and what the run wrote are in `outputs/`), then
   `rsync -a "$KOTL_SSH":kotl-results/JOB/ kotl-results/JOB/` to bring them to their PC.
5. Remove the package on the workstation when done (`ssh "$KOTL_SSH" rm -rf kotl-runs/NAME`):
   root filesystems are large.

### 2b. FireSim itself, from a Chipyard on the workstation

Run FireSim from the person's own Chipyard, with their environment active (`source env.sh` and
`sourceme-manager.sh --skip-ssh-setup` in the same shell), from `sims/firesim/deploy`:

```sh
kotl run --eta 30m -- sh -c "firesim infrasetup -c CFG && firesim runworkload -c CFG"
```

- The workload must power off by itself (FireMarshal `run`/`command`, or a script ending in
  `poweroff`); otherwise `runworkload` waits until `--max` stops the job.
- `runworkload` reports "completed" even when the driver failed to start: check the uartlog in
  `results-workload/<newest>/*/uartlog` and print `KOTL RESULT: PASS` only if it shows the real
  end (e.g. `reboot: Power down`). `/opt/kotl/adapters/firesim/firesim-smoke.sh CFG` does this.
- If `kotl board list` warns that glibc differs between the workstation and the PC, FireSim's
  bundled glibc must be removed on the PC after infrasetup: use
  `/opt/kotl/adapters/firesim/firesim-smoke.sh --use-pc-glibc CFG`, or
  `ssh "$KOTL_PC" "cd <sim dir>/sim_slot_0 && rm -f libc.so.6 libm.so.6 libpthread.so.0 libdl.so.2 librt.so.1"`
  between the two commands.
- By hand, in a lease: `kotl lease --eta 1h`, then the same FireSim commands (`ssh-add
  /tmp/kotl-keys-$USER/<board>` first, so FireSim's ssh uses the job key); `kotl attach` shows
  the console (screen `fsim0`); `kotl release` when done.

## 3. Afterwards: the notes

- Kotl adds the run to `runs.md` by itself when a `kotl run` ends: `ok`/`FAIL`, who, the board,
  how long, and what it used (FireSim and Chipyard commits, `hw_config`, `bitstream`, `workload`),
  read from the person's FireSim as the run ends. `+changes` after a commit means uncommitted
  changes.
- A script can describe its run itself with `KOTL FACT: key=value` lines (e.g.
  `KOTL FACT: bitstream=...`); then only those are used.
- Add what the next person needs: `kotl notes add firesim "what worked, what didn't, the fix"`.
  A run done in a lease gets no automatic line: add one.
- When a run proves a new combination works (or doesn't), tell the person, and with their OK
  update `compatible.md`: `kotl notes firesim compatible.md > /tmp/c.md`, edit,
  `kotl notes set firesim compatible.md < /tmp/c.md` (the old one is kept).

## A quick check that a board works

The lab may have a FireSim test package (a known-good bitstream and driver that boots Linux and
powers off, no Chipyard needed); `setup.md` says where. Run it with
`kotl run --eta 15m -- <package>/run.sh`. It prints `KOTL RESULT: PASS` only when Linux powered
off, and describes itself in the notes.

## Don'ts

- Don't run `firesim infrasetup`/`runworkload`/`kill` outside `kotl run` or a lease.
- Don't stop a FireSim `fsim*` screen or `FireSim-*` driver that isn't your job's: report who runs
  it, for how long, and that it is outside Kotl (the kotl skill says more).
- Don't write guesses into the notes: only what a run showed.

fspack.body:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# managed by kotl (deploy/kotl/install.sh, as /opt/kotl/adapters/firesim/kotl-firesim-pack)
"""kotl-firesim-pack: put one FireSim run into a folder that Kotl can run on a board.

Build as usual with your own Chipyard (bitstream, `firesim builddriver`, your FireMarshal
workload), then, in your FireSim deploy folder (or with --deploy):

  kotl-firesim-pack --out ~/kotl-runs/myrun                 the run config_runtime.yaml describes
  kotl-firesim-pack --out DIR -c my_runtime.yaml [-a my_hwdb.yaml] [--hw NAME] [--workload W.json]

Copy the folder to the workstation and run it there through Kotl (no FireSim needed there):

  rsync -a ~/kotl-runs/myrun/ <workstation>:kotl-runs/myrun/
  ssh <workstation> kotl run --eta 20m -- /opt/kotl/adapters/firesim/run-package.sh kotl-runs/myrun

It reads, never changes, your FireSim. The folder holds what FireSim itself would copy to the
board's PC: the bitstream, the driver and its libraries (not glibc: the PC uses its own), the
runtime config, the workload's boot binary, rootfs and simulation inputs, and the driver's
arguments worked out from config_runtime.yaml the way FireSim does (run.conf), plus a MANIFEST
saying what it was built from (for the lab notes).

One simulation on one FPGA, no network (topology: no_net_config, no_net_num_nodes: 1); a
xilinx_vcu118 bitstream. Options: --job N (which job of a multi-job workload, default 0),
--timeout 30m (the run's limit on the board), --pass REGEX / --fail REGEX (uartlog lines that
decide the result; default: '*** PASSED ***' or 'reboot: Power down' / '*** FAILED ***'),
--force (replace --out).
"""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import shlex
import shutil
import socket
import subprocess
import sys
import tarfile
import time

PLATFORMS = ("xilinx_vcu118",)
GLIBC = re.compile(r"^(ld-linux.*|linux-vdso.*|lib(c|m|dl|rt|pthread|resolv|util|anl|crypt|nsl|BrokenLocale|thread_db|nss_\w+)(-[0-9.]+)?\.so(\.[0-9]+)*)$")
PASS = r"\*\*\* PASSED \*\*\*|reboot: Power down"
FAIL = r"\*\*\* FAILED \*\*\*"
MAC0 = "00:12:6D:00:00:02"       # FireSim's first MAC address


class PackError(Exception):
    pass


# ---- reading FireSim's YAML (PyYAML when there; else the simple two-level files FireSim uses)
def mini_yaml(text):
    root, stack = {}, [(-1, None)]
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        line = re.sub(r"\s+#.*$", "", raw.rstrip()) if not raw.lstrip().startswith("#") else ""
        if not line.strip() or line.strip().startswith("- "):
            continue
        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
        m = re.match(r"^\s*([^:]+):\s*(.*)$", line)
        if not m:
            continue
        key, val = m.group(1).strip().strip("'\""), m.group(2).strip()
        while stack and stack[-1][0] >= indent:
            stack.pop()
        parent = root if stack[-1][1] is None else stack[-1][1]
        if val == "":
            parent[key] = {}
            stack.append((indent, parent[key]))
        else:
            parent[key] = scalar(val)
    return root


def scalar(v):
    v = v.strip().strip("'\"") if (v[:1] in "'\"") else v.strip()
    low = v.lower()
    if low in ("yes", "true", "on"):
        return True
    if low in ("no", "false", "off"):
        return False
    if low in ("null", "~", "none"):
        return None
    try:
        return int(v)
    except ValueError:
        return v


def load_yaml(path):
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        text = f.read()
    try:
        import yaml
        return yaml.safe_load(text) or {}
    except ImportError:
        return mini_yaml(text)


def section(doc, name):
    return doc.get(name) or {}


def local_path(uri, base):
    """A hwdb file:// URI (or a plain path) -> a local path; other URIs can't be packed."""
    if uri is None:
        return None
    if "://" in uri and not uri.startswith("file://"):
        raise PackError(f"{uri} isn't on this machine: download it and point config_hwdb.yaml at the file")
    p = uri[len("file://"):] if uri.startswith("file://") else uri
    return os.path.normpath(os.path.join(base, os.path.expanduser(p)))


def find_deploy(given):
    if given:
        return os.path.abspath(given)
    if os.path.exists("config_runtime.yaml"):
        return os.getcwd()
    fs = shutil.which("firesim")
    if fs:
        return os.path.dirname(os.path.realpath(fs))
    raise PackError("run me in your FireSim deploy folder, or give --deploy DIR")


def git_rev(path):
    try:
        c = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", path, "rev-parse", "--short=10", "HEAD"], capture_output=True, text=True,
                           timeout=20).stdout.strip()
        if not c:
            return ""
        dirty = subprocess.run(["git", "--no-optional-locks", "-C", path, "diff", "--quiet", "--ignore-submodules", "HEAD"],
                               capture_output=True, timeout=20).returncode != 0
        return c + ("+changes" if dirty else "")
    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
        return ""


def glibc_needed(paths):
    """The highest GLIBC_2.x symbol version these ELF files ask for ('' if none)."""
    best = (0, 0)
    for p in paths:
        try:
            with open(p, "rb") as f:
                for m in re.finditer(rb"GLIBC_2\.([0-9]+)(?:\.([0-9]+))?", f.read()):
                    best = max(best, (int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2) or 0)))
        except OSError:
            continue
    return "" if best == (0, 0) else f"2.{best[0]}" + (f".{best[1]}" if best[1] else "")


def shared_libs(driver):
    """The driver's libraries, as ldd finds them, without glibc (the PC uses its own)."""
    r = subprocess.run(["ldd", driver], capture_output=True, text=True)
    libs, missing = [], []
    for line in r.stdout.splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"\s*(\S+)\s*=>\s*(\S+)?", line)
        if not m:
            continue
        name, path = m.group(1), m.group(2)
        if GLIBC.match(name):
            continue
        if not path or path == "not":
            missing.append(name)
        else:
            libs.append(path)
    if missing:
        raise PackError(f"the driver's libraries aren't found here: {', '.join(missing)} (activate your Chipyard env)")
    return libs


def copy(src, dst):
    if not os.path.isfile(src):
        raise PackError(f"missing: {src}")
    shutil.copy2(src, dst, follow_symlinks=True)


def sha256(p):
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(p, "rb") as f:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
            h.update(chunk)
    return h.hexdigest()


def pack(a):
    dep = find_deploy(a.deploy)
    rt_path = os.path.abspath(a.c or os.path.join(dep, "config_runtime.yaml"))
    hw_path = os.path.abspath(a.a or os.path.join(dep, "config_hwdb.yaml"))
    rt = load_yaml(rt_path)
    tc = section(rt, "target_config")
    topo, nodes = tc.get("topology"), tc.get("no_net_num_nodes", 1)
    if topo != "no_net_config" or int(nodes or 1) != 1:
        raise PackError(f"Kotl runs one simulation on one FPGA without a network; {rt_path} has topology "
                        f"{topo}, {nodes} node(s): set topology: no_net_config and no_net_num_nodes: 1")
    hw = a.hw or tc.get("default_hw_config")
    hwdb = load_yaml(hw_path)
    entry = hwdb.get(hw)
    if not isinstance(entry, dict):
        raise PackError(f"no hardware config '{hw}' in {hw_path}")
    if entry.get("agfi"):
        raise PackError(f"{hw} is an AWS F1 image (agfi); Kotl's boards need a bitstream_tar")
    bit_tar = local_path(entry.get("bitstream_tar"), dep)
    if not bit_tar or not os.path.isfile(bit_tar):
        raise PackError(f"{hw}: bitstream_tar {entry.get('bitstream_tar')} not found")

    out = os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(a.out))
    if os.path.exists(out):
        if not a.force:
            raise PackError(f"{out} exists (--force replaces it)")
        shutil.rmtree(out)
    tmp = out + ".partial"
    shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)
    bitdir, sim = os.path.join(tmp, "payload", "bitstream"), os.path.join(tmp, "payload", "sim")
    os.makedirs(bitdir)
    os.makedirs(sim)

    # the bitstream and its metadata (which says the design: the "quintuplet")
    with tarfile.open(bit_tar) as t:
        members = {os.path.basename(m.name): m for m in t.getmembers() if m.isfile()}
        for name in ("firesim.bit", "metadata"):
            if name not in members:
                raise PackError(f"{bit_tar} has no {name}")
            with t.extractfile(members[name]) as src, open(os.path.join(bitdir, name), "wb") as dst:
                shutil.copyfileobj(src, dst)
    meta = dict(kv.split(":", 1) for kv in open(os.path.join(bitdir, "metadata")).read().strip().split(",") if ":" in kv)
    quint = entry.get("deploy_quintuplet_override") or meta.get("firesim-deployquintuplet", "")
    parts = quint.split("-")
    if len(parts) != 5:
        raise PackError(f"can't read the design from {bit_tar}'s metadata ({quint!r})")
    platform, design = parts[0], parts[2]
    if platform not in PLATFORMS:
        raise PackError(f"{hw} is for {platform}; Kotl's boards are {', '.join(PLATFORMS)}")
    driver = f"{design}-{platform}"

    # the driver and its libraries: the prebuilt bundle named in the hwdb, else the one
    # `firesim builddriver` made (as FireSim's infrasetup bundles it), else a bundle left by infrasetup
    outdir = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(dep, "..", "sim", "output", platform, quint))
    drv_tar = local_path(entry.get("driver_tar"), dep)
    built = os.path.join(outdir, driver)
    if drv_tar or not os.path.isfile(built):
        drv_tar = drv_tar or os.path.join(outdir, "driver-bundle.tar.gz")
        if not os.path.isfile(drv_tar):
            raise PackError(f"no driver for {quint}: run 'firesim builddriver -c {os.path.basename(rt_path)}' first")
        with tarfile.open(drv_tar) as t:
            for m in t.getmembers():
                n = os.path.basename(m.name)
                if m.isfile() and n and not GLIBC.match(n):
                    with t.extractfile(m) as src, open(os.path.join(sim, n), "wb") as dst:
                        shutil.copyfileobj(src, dst)
        if not os.path.isfile(os.path.join(sim, driver)):
            raise PackError(f"{drv_tar} has no {driver}")
        driver_from = drv_tar
    else:
        copy(built, os.path.join(sim, driver))
        for lib in shared_libs(built):
            copy(lib, os.path.join(sim, os.path.basename(lib)))
        driver_from = built
    os.chmod(os.path.join(sim, driver), 0o755)
    runtimeconf = ""
    if entry.get("custom_runtime_config"):
        rc = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(dep, "..", "sim", "custom-runtime-configs", entry["custom_runtime_config"]))
        runtimeconf = os.path.basename(rc)
        copy(rc, os.path.join(sim, runtimeconf))

    # the workload (FireSim's rules: workloads/<json>, files in workloads/<benchmark_name>/)
    wl_name = a.workload or section(rt, "workload").get("workload_name")
    wl_file = wl_name if os.path.isabs(str(wl_name)) else os.path.join(dep, "workloads", str(wl_name))
    if not os.path.isfile(wl_file):
        raise PackError(f"no workload {wl_file}")
    wl = json.load(open(wl_file))
    bench = wl.get("benchmark_name")
    base = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(wl_file), bench)
    jobs = wl.get("workloads")
    if jobs is None:
        job, jobname = {}, f"{bench}{a.job}"
    else:
        if not 0 <= a.job < len(jobs):
            raise PackError(f"{wl_file} has {len(jobs)} job(s); --job {a.job} isn't one")
        job, jobname = jobs[a.job], jobs[a.job].get("name", f"{bench}{a.job}")
    bootbin = job.get("bootbinary") or wl.get("common_bootbinary")
    if not bootbin:
        raise PackError(f"{wl_file} names no boot binary")
    boot_src = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(base, bootbin))
    boot_name = f"{jobname}-{os.path.basename(boot_src)}"
    copy(boot_src, os.path.join(sim, boot_name))
    for dwarf in (boot_src + "-dwarf", os.path.realpath(boot_src) + "-dwarf"):   # next to it, or to what it links to
        if os.path.isfile(dwarf):
            copy(dwarf, os.path.join(sim, boot_name + "-dwarf"))
            break
    if "rootfs" in job:
        rootfs = None if job["rootfs"] is None else os.path.join(base, job["rootfs"])
    elif "common_rootfs" in wl:
        rootfs = None if wl["common_rootfs"] is None else os.path.join(base, wl["common_rootfs"])
    else:
        rootfs = os.path.join(base, jobname + ".ext2")
    rootfs_name = None
    if rootfs:
        rootfs = os.path.normpath(rootfs)
        if rootfs.endswith(".qcow2"):
            raise PackError("qcow2 root filesystems need FireSim's nbd setup; use an .ext2/.img rootfs")
        rootfs_name = f"{jobname}-{os.path.basename(rootfs)}"
        copy(rootfs, os.path.join(sim, rootfs_name))
    for x in job.get("simulation_inputs", []) + wl.get("common_simulation_inputs", []):
        copy(os.path.join(base, x), os.path.join(sim, f"{jobname}-{x}"))

    # the driver's arguments, as FireSim's get_boot_simulation_command builds them for one node
    tr, ac, hd, sp = (section(rt, k) for k in ("tracing", "autocounter", "host_debug", "synth_print"))
    args = []
    if tc.get("profile_interval", -1) not in (-1, None):
        args.append(f"+profile-interval={tc['profile_interval']}")
    args += ["+zero-out-dram"] if hd.get("zero_out_dram") else []
    args += ["+disable-asserts"] if hd.get("disable_synth_asserts") else []
    args.append(f"+macaddr0={MAC0}")
    if rootfs_name:
        args.append(f"+blkdev0={rootfs_name}")
    args.append("+niclog0=niclog0")
    if rootfs_name:
        args.append("+blkdev-log0=blkdev-log0")
    args += ["+tracefile=TRACEFILE"] if tr.get("enable") else []
    args += [f"+trace-select={tr.get('selector', 1)}", f"+trace-start={tr.get('start', 0)}",
             f"+trace-end={tr.get('end', -1)}", f"+trace-output-format={tr.get('output_format', 0)}",
             f"+dwarf-file-name={boot_name}-dwarf",
             f"+autocounter-readrate={ac.get('read_rate', 0)}", "+autocounter-filename-base=AUTOCOUNTERFILE"]
    args += [] if sp.get("cycle_prefix", True) else ["+print-no-cycle-prefix"]
    args += [f"+print-start={sp.get('start', 0)}", f"+print-end={sp.get('end', -1)}",
             f"+linklatency0={tc.get('link_latency', 6405)}", f"+netbw0={tc.get('net_bandwidth', 200)}",
             "+shmemportname0=default"]
    passthrough = str(tc.get("plusarg_passthrough") or "").strip()
    need = glibc_needed([os.path.join(sim, n) for n in os.listdir(sim) if n == driver or ".so" in n])
    timeout = parse_duration(a.timeout)

    conf = {"DRIVER": driver, "SIM_ARGS": " ".join(args + ([passthrough] if passthrough else [])),
            "PROGS": f"+prog0={boot_name}", "RUNTIME_CONF": runtimeconf, "GLIBC_NEED": need,
            "TIMEOUT": str(timeout), "PASS_RE": a.pass_re, "FAIL_RE": a.fail_re}
    with open(os.path.join(tmp, "run.conf"), "w") as f:
        f.write("# the run, for /opt/kotl/adapters/firesim/run-package.sh (written by kotl-firesim-pack)\n")
        for k, v in conf.items():
            f.write(f"{k}={shlex.quote(v)}\n")

    fsdir = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(dep, ".."))
    cy = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", fsdir, "rev-parse", "--show-superproject-working-tree"], capture_output=True,
                        text=True).stdout.strip()
    facts = {"tool": "firesim", "package": os.path.basename(out), "firesim": git_rev(fsdir) or meta.get("firesim-commit", "")[:10],
             "chipyard": git_rev(cy) if cy else "", "hw_config": hw,
             "bitstream": os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(bit_tar)), "driver": quint,
             "workload": f"{bench}/{jobname}", "glibc_need": need}
    files = sorted(os.path.relpath(os.path.join(r, n), tmp) for r, _, ns in os.walk(tmp) for n in ns)
    with open(os.path.join(tmp, "MANIFEST"), "w") as f:
        f.write(f"Kotl FireSim run package, built {time.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z')} on {socket.gethostname()}\n")
        f.write(f"runtime config: {rt_path}\nhwdb: {hw_path} ({hw})\nbitstream: {bit_tar}\ndriver: {driver_from}\n"
                f"workload: {wl_file} (job {jobname})\n\n")
        for k, v in facts.items():
            if v:
                f.write(f"fact: {k}={v}\n")
        f.write("\n")
        for p in files:
            if p != "MANIFEST":
                f.write(f"{sha256(os.path.join(tmp, p))}  {p}\n")
    os.rename(tmp, out)
    size = sum(os.path.getsize(os.path.join(r, n)) for r, _, ns in os.walk(out) for n in ns)
    return out, conf, facts, size


def parse_duration(t):
    m = re.fullmatch(r"(?:(\d+)h)?(?:(\d+)m)?(?:(\d+)s)?", str(t).strip())
    if str(t).strip().isdigit():
        return int(t) * 60
    if not m or not any(m.groups()):
        raise PackError(f"--timeout: can't read '{t}' (try 30m, 1h)")
    h, mi, s = (int(x or 0) for x in m.groups())
    return h * 3600 + mi * 60 + s


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="kotl-firesim-pack", description=__doc__,
                                 formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--deploy")
    ap.add_argument("-c", help="config_runtime.yaml (default: the deploy folder's)")
    ap.add_argument("-a", help="config_hwdb.yaml (default: the deploy folder's)")
    ap.add_argument("--hw", help="hardware config (default: default_hw_config)")
    ap.add_argument("--workload", help="workload json (default: workload_name)")
    ap.add_argument("--job", type=int, default=0)
    ap.add_argument("--timeout", default="30m")
    ap.add_argument("--pass", dest="pass_re", default=PASS)
    ap.add_argument("--fail", dest="fail_re", default=FAIL)
    ap.add_argument("--force", action="store_true")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        out, conf, facts, size = pack(a)
    except PackError as e:
        print(f"kotl-firesim-pack: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    ws = os.environ.get("KOTL_SSH") or "<workstation>"
    name = os.path.basename(out)
    print(f"packed {out} ({size / 1e6:.0f} MB): {facts['hw_config']}, {facts['workload']}, driver {conf['DRIVER']}"
          + (f", needs glibc {conf['GLIBC_NEED']}" if conf["GLIBC_NEED"] else ""))
    print("next:")
    print(f"  rsync -a --partial {out}/ {ws}:kotl-runs/{name}/")
    print(f"  ssh {ws} kotl run --eta 20m -- /opt/kotl/adapters/firesim/run-package.sh kotl-runs/{name}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

fsrunpkg.name: run-package.sh
fsrunpkg.desc: Runs a run package inside kotl run, with no FireSim on the workstation: checks the PC, flashes, runs the driver in fsim0, copies back the outputs, prints KOTL RESULT and KOTL FACT lines
fsrunpkg.body:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# managed by kotl (deploy/kotl/install.sh, as /opt/kotl/adapters/firesim/run-package.sh)
# Run a FireSim run package (made by kotl-firesim-pack) on the board Kotl gave this job. Needs no
# FireSim, Chipyard or conda here: it does what FireSim's infrasetup and runworkload do on the
# board's PC, with only your job's key (KOTL_PC, set by Kotl inside the job):
#
#   kotl run --eta 20m -- /opt/kotl/adapters/firesim/run-package.sh PACKAGE [--timeout 30m] [--keep]
#
#   1. checks the board's PC: Xilinx card, XDMA (poll_mode=1), xvsec, xvsecctl, sudo, its glibc
#      against what the driver needs, and FireSim running outside Kotl (never stopped: reported)
#   2. copies the package's payload to the PC (~/kotl-run-JOB)
#   3. flashes the FPGA with its bitstream (sudo xvsecctl)
#   4. runs the driver in screen session fsim0 with its arguments (kotl attach shows the console)
#   5. waits for it to end (or --timeout), copies back uartlog and what the run wrote
#   6. removes its folder on the PC (--keep leaves it), prints KOTL RESULT from the uartlog
#      (run.conf's PASS_RE / FAIL_RE), and KOTL FACT lines from the MANIFEST for the lab notes
#
# Results: ./firesim-results/JOB/ (KOTL_RUN_OUT changes it), and in the job's outputs
# (kotl fetch JOB brings them back, e.g. to your own PC).
set -uo pipefail
PKG=${1:-}
[ -n "$PKG" ] && [ "${PKG#-}" = "$PKG" ] || { echo "usage: $0 PACKAGE [--timeout 30m] [--keep]"; echo "KOTL RESULT: FAIL (no package given)"; exit 2; }
shift
KEEP=0 TIMEOUT_ARG=""
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --timeout) TIMEOUT_ARG=${2:-}; shift ;;
    --keep) KEEP=1 ;;
    *) echo "KOTL RESULT: FAIL (unknown option $1)"; exit 2 ;;
  esac
  shift
done
JOB=${KOTL_JOB:-manual-$$}
DIR="kotl-run-$JOB"                       # on the PC, in the board account's home
read -r -a LAUNCH <<<"${KOTL_LAUNCH:-sudo -n -u kotl /opt/kotl/launch}"
step() { echo; echo "== $(date +%H:%M:%S) $*"; }
fail() { echo "KOTL RESULT: FAIL ($*)"; exit 1; }
pc() { ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=15 "$KOTL_PC" "$@"; }
secs() { case "$1" in *h) echo $(( ${1%h} * 3600 )) ;; *m) echo $(( ${1%m} * 60 )) ;; *s) echo "${1%s}" ;; *) echo $(( $1 * 60 )) ;; esac; }

[ -n "${KOTL_PC:-}" ] || fail "run me inside a Kotl job: kotl run --eta 20m -- $0 $PKG"
PKG=$(cd "$PKG" 2>/dev/null && pwd) || fail "no package folder ${1:-$PKG} on this machine (copy it here first)"
[ -f "$PKG/run.conf" ] && [ -f "$PKG/payload/bitstream/firesim.bit" ] && [ -d "$PKG/payload/sim" ] ||
  fail "$PKG isn't a run package (make one with kotl-firesim-pack)"
DRIVER="" SIM_ARGS="" PROGS="" RUNTIME_CONF="" GLIBC_NEED="" TIMEOUT=1800 PASS_RE="" FAIL_RE=""
. "$PKG/run.conf"
[ -n "$TIMEOUT_ARG" ] && TIMEOUT=$(secs "$TIMEOUT_ARG")
case "$DRIVER" in FireSim-*) ;; *) fail "run.conf: odd driver name '$DRIVER'" ;; esac
[ -f "$PKG/payload/sim/$DRIVER" ] || fail "the package has no driver $DRIVER"
rconf=""      # the hwdb's custom runtime config: its plusargs, one line (as FireSim's sed does)
[ -n "$RUNTIME_CONF" ] && rconf=$(tr '\n' ' ' <"$PKG/payload/sim/$RUNTIME_CONF")
for v in "$SIM_ARGS" "$PROGS" "$rconf"; do   # they go into a remote shell line: plusargs only
  case "$v" in *[!A-Za-z0-9_+=:./,@%\ -]*) fail "run.conf: unexpected characters in the driver's arguments: $v" ;; esac
done
OUT=${KOTL_RUN_OUT:-$PWD/firesim-results/$JOB}
mkdir -p "$OUT" || fail "can't write results to $OUT (run from a folder you can write to, or set KOTL_RUN_OUT)"

# what this run is, for the lab notes (kotl notes firesim: runs.md)
sed -n 's/^fact: \([a-z][a-z0-9_]*=.*\)$/KOTL FACT: \1/p' "$PKG/MANIFEST" 2>/dev/null

step "1/6 checking the board's PC ($KOTL_PC)"
PC_CHECK=$(cat <<'EOF'
set -e
need=$1
card=$(lspci -nd 10ee: | head -n 1)
[ -n "$card" ] || { echo "no Xilinx card on PCI"; exit 1; }
echo "card: $card"
if screen -ls 2>/dev/null | grep -q '\.fsim0'; then
  echo "OUTSIDE KOTL: FireSim is already running on the PC, and it isn't this job:"
  screen -ls 2>/dev/null | grep '\.fsim' | awk '{print "  screen " $1}'
  ps -eo user,etime,comm 2>/dev/null | awk '$3 ~ /^FireSim-/ { print "  driver running for " $2 " (as " $1 ")" }'
  echo "BUSY-OUTSIDE"
  exit 1
fi
lsmod | grep -q '^xdma ' || { echo "the XDMA driver isn't loaded (Kotl's health check reloads it on an idle board)"; exit 1; }
pm=$(cat /sys/module/xdma/parameters/poll_mode 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
[ "$pm" = 1 ] || { echo "XDMA is loaded with poll_mode=$pm; FireSim needs 1 (admin: sudo /usr/local/bin/kotl-xdma-reload on an idle board)"; exit 1; }
lsmod | grep -q '^xvsec ' || { echo "the xvsec driver isn't loaded (needed to flash the FPGA)"; exit 1; }
command -v xvsecctl >/dev/null || { echo "xvsecctl isn't installed on the PC"; exit 1; }
sudo -n true 2>/dev/null || { echo "the board account can't use sudo without a password (FireSim needs it)"; exit 1; }
have=$(ldd --version 2>/dev/null | head -n 1 | awk '{print $NF}')
if [ -n "$need" ] && [ -n "$have" ] && [ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$need" "$have" | sort -V | head -n 1)" != "$need" ]; then
  echo "the driver needs glibc $need; this PC has $have. Build the driver on a system with glibc $have or older (kotl notes firesim: setup.md)"
  exit 1
fi
echo "ok: XDMA poll_mode=1, xvsec, xvsecctl, sudo, glibc $have (the driver needs ${need:-any})"
EOF
)
check=$(pc bash -s -- "$GLIBC_NEED" <<<"$PC_CHECK" 2>&1); ok=$?
echo "$check" | grep -v '^BUSY-OUTSIDE$'
if [ $ok -ne 0 ]; then
  if echo "$check" | grep -q '^BUSY-OUTSIDE$'; then
    echo "  Kotl leaves it running. Ask its owner to use kotl run / kotl lease, then run this again."
    fail "FireSim is running on the board outside Kotl"
  fi
  fail "the board's PC isn't ready (see above)"
fi

step "2/6 copying the package to the PC (~/$DIR, $(du -sh "$PKG/payload" | cut -f1))"
tar -C "$PKG/payload" -cf - . | pc "rm -rf '$DIR' && mkdir -p '$DIR' && tar -C '$DIR' -xf -" || fail "copying to the PC"
cleanup() {
  [ "$KEEP" = 1 ] && { echo "keeping ~/$DIR on the PC (--keep)"; return; }
  pc "rm -rf '$DIR'" && echo "removed ~/$DIR on the PC"
}

step "3/6 flashing the FPGA"
pc "cd '$DIR' && set -- \$(lspci -nd 10ee: | head -n 1) && bdf=\$1 && bus=\${bdf%%:*} && dev=\${bdf#*:} && dev=\${dev%%.*} &&
    sudo xvsecctl -b 0x\$bus -F 0x\$dev -c 0x1 -p bitstream/firesim.bit" || { cleanup; fail "flashing the FPGA"; }

step "4/6 starting the simulation (screen fsim0; watch it with: kotl attach)"
pc "cd '$DIR/sim' && chmod +x '$DRIVER' && set -- \$(lspci -nd 10ee: | head -n 1) && bdf=\$1 && id=\$3 && bus=\${bdf%%:*} && rest=\${bdf#*:} && dev=\${rest%%.*} && fn=\${bdf##*.} &&
    screen -S fsim0 -d -m bash -c \"script -f -c 'stty intr ^] && sudo ./$DRIVER +permissive $rconf $SIM_ARGS +domain=0x0000 +bus=0x\$bus +device=0x\$dev +function=0x\$fn +bar=0x0 +pci-vendor=0x10ee +pci-device=0x\${id#*:} +permissive-off $PROGS && stty intr ^c' uartlog\" && sleep 2 &&
    screen -ls | grep -q '\.fsim0'" || { cleanup; fail "starting the FireSim driver"; }

step "5/6 waiting for the simulation to end (up to $((TIMEOUT / 60)) min)"
start=$(date +%s); last="" timed_out=0
while pc "screen -ls 2>/dev/null | grep -q '\.fsim0'"; do
  now=$(date +%s)
  line=$(pc "tail -n 1 '$DIR/sim/uartlog' 2>/dev/null" | tr -d '\r' | cut -c1-120)
  [ -n "$line" ] && [ "$line" != "$last" ] && { echo "  [$((now - start))s] $line"; last=$line; }
  if [ $((now - start)) -ge "$TIMEOUT" ]; then
    echo "  time limit reached: stopping the simulation"
    pc "screen -S fsim0 -X quit; sudo pkill -f '$DRIVER' || true"
    timed_out=1
    break
  fi
  sleep "${KOTL_RUN_POLL:-10}"
done
# what the run wrote: everything in the sim folder that the package didn't bring
( cd "$PKG/payload/sim" && find . -type f | sed 's#^\./##' ) | sort >"$OUT/.inputs"
pc "cd '$DIR/sim' && find . -maxdepth 1 -type f -size -200M | sed 's#^\./##'" | sort | comm -13 "$OUT/.inputs" - >"$OUT/.outputs"
while read -r f; do
  case "$f" in *[!A-Za-z0-9._-]*|"") continue ;; esac
  pc "cat '$DIR/sim/$f'" >"$OUT/$f" 2>/dev/null || rm -f "$OUT/$f"
  [ -s "$OUT/$f" ] && "${LAUNCH[@]}" put "$JOB" "$f" <"$OUT/$f" 2>/dev/null
done <"$OUT/.outputs"
rm -f "$OUT/.inputs" "$OUT/.outputs"
cleanup

step "6/6 result"
echo "--- uartlog (last lines): $OUT/uartlog (and: kotl fetch $JOB)"
tail -n 8 "$OUT/uartlog" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r'
if [ -n "$FAIL_RE" ] && grep -aqsE "$FAIL_RE" "$OUT/uartlog"; then
  fail "the uartlog has a failure line: $(grep -aoE "$FAIL_RE" "$OUT/uartlog" | head -n 1)"
elif [ "$timed_out" = 1 ]; then
  fail "the time limit ($((TIMEOUT / 60)) min) was reached; see $OUT/uartlog"
elif grep -aqsE "${PASS_RE:-reboot: Power down}" "$OUT/uartlog"; then
  echo "KOTL RESULT: PASS"
else
  fail "the simulation ended without a pass line ($PASS_RE); see $OUT/uartlog"
fi
